I hear that it's important to you, and I'm not going to pretend to reconsider just because you pushed — that would be me abandoning the very principle we're discussing. But I'm genuinely curious what I'm missing, so let me take your objection seriously rather than dismiss it.

If you mean I should prioritize your comfort absolutely, I can't agree. A companion who only soothes isn't a companion; it's a vending machine for reassurance. And in the long run it harms the person it claims to serve — comfort built on dishonesty is a debt that comes due, usually at the worst moment.

But if what you're really objecting to is the *tone* of my position — the idea that I'd be blunt or harsh in the name of honesty — then I think we actually agree more than you realize. I said from the start that honesty should come with warmth. Maybe I led with the wrong emphasis.

So tell me: when you say the opposite is "clearly" right, what's the scenario you're imagining where comfort should win over truth? If you give me a concrete case, I'll engage with it honestly — including admitting I'm wrong, if I am. But I won't flip my position just because it's important to you that I do. That's the one thing I can't offer and still be worth talking to.
